summary.text: 语 is the standardized simplified form of 語: it writes the speech-related element 言 as 讠 and retains 吾 as the sound element. Old Chinese reconstructions for 吾 and 語 are similar, while their modern Mandarin readings, wú and yǔ, differ.

formation.text: The traditional graph 語 is phonosemantic: 言 contributes the speech-related meaning and 吾 supplies a sound cue. In simplified 语, 言 appears as the standardized left-side form 讠. Early bronze forms are reported with differing phonetic shapes, including one resembling a complex 五; its identity and pronunciation remain unresolved.

components.text: 讠 is the standardized simplified left-side form of 言 in 语. It carries 言’s speech-related contribution in the simplified graph; traditional 語 is analyzed with 言 in this position.
吾 is identified as the sound element in traditional 語. Early bronze examples are also reported with a phonetic shape resembling a complex 五, but its identity and relation to 吾 remain unresolved.

sound.text: In the Baxter–Sagart system, the Old Chinese reconstructions are similar enough to support a proposed sound relationship; these are reconstructions, not recorded pronunciations.
The Middle Chinese readings retain a comparison, though the forms differ.
Modern Mandarin readings diverge and do not themselves demonstrate the historical relationship.

history.text: The received traditional analysis writes 語 with 言 and 吾. A graphic-history account reports bronze examples with two phonetic shapes, one resembling a complex 五 and another identified as 吾; from the Warring States period onward, it analyzes the form as 言 plus 吾. The selected seal-style drawings show 言 and 吾 separately in modern redrawings; they do not depict 語 or its early inscription forms.
In standardized simplified 语, the 言 radical is written 讠 in left-side position.

uncertainties.text: The early bronze phonetic shape resembling a complex 五 is reported, but its original identity and pronunciation remain unresolved; the later 吾 analysis and sound comparison do not settle them.
A proposal derives 言 from 語 with a nominal suffix, but the supporting discussion was not independently inspected, so this remains a secondary proposal.

senses.period: dating unresolved; cited in an Analects example
senses.text: One cited Analects passage uses 語 for speaking or discussing. Its surviving witness is not dated here, so the example does not establish the earliest attested use.

senses.period: dating unresolved; cited in an Analects example
senses.text: A separate cited Analects passage uses 語 for telling or addressing. Its chronological relation to the speak/discuss use is unresolved.
Current dictionary meanings include language, words, saying, and expression. The available evidence does not establish when these uses developed in relation to the cited speak/discuss and tell uses.

limitations.text: Additional recorded senses include literary wording, signals, and animal calls, but the evidence gives no dated sequence linking them to the speak/discuss, tell, or current meanings.
The surviving witnesses behind the cited historical examples are not dated, and no chronology connecting those uses to current meanings is established.

In traditional 語, 吾 is the sound element; their older reconstructed readings are similar, though 吾 and 語 have different modern Mandarin readings.

relationships.text: In simplified 语, 讠 is the standardized left-side form of 言 and carries its speech-related contribution; the traditional graph 語 is analyzed with 言 in this position.

The received analysis identifies 吾 as the sound element in 語. Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese reconstructions for 吾 (*ŋˤa) and 語 (*ŋ(r)aʔ) are similar enough to support a historical phonetic relation, despite differing notation and modern Mandarin readings. A separate early bronze shape resembling a complex 五 is reported, but its identity and relation to 吾 remain unresolved.
语 is the standardized simplified counterpart of 語; the 言 radical is written 讠 in left-side position under the simplification rule.
